2. This application is filed against the order dated Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.38842 of 2019(22) dt.29-01-2026 10.01.2019 passed in Criminal Revision No. 33 of 2018 by the Sessions Judge, Gaya, affirming the order dated 24.01.2018 passed by the learned SDJM, Gaya in G.R. No.

3.
sentences._hearing_file: Sanjay Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 29 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: The summarized facts of the case is that one Rampur P.S. Case No. 243 of 2016 was registered under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code and under Section  of the D.P. Act on the written petition filed by the opposite party no. 02.
sentences._hearing_file: Sanjay Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 29 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: Thereafter, the petitioner approached this Court and was granted provisional bail by this Court vide order dated 15.05.2017 passed in Cr. Misc. No. 3083 of 2017.
sentences._hearing_file: Sanjay Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 29 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: The petitioner appeared before the Court below for furnishing his bail bonds and thereafter the SDJM, Gaya, upon execution of bail bonds, was granted bail provisionally for a period of six months and 1.8.2017 was fixed by the Court below for hearing.
sentences._hearing_file: Sanjay Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 29 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: On 1.8.2017, the informant submitted that she was not properly treated by her in-laws and therefore, the learned SDJM, Gaya cancelled the bail bonds of the petitioner on 24.01.2018, as the same was granted with a condition that the petitioner will keep his wife with full dignity and care.
sentences._hearing_file: Sanjay Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 29 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: The petitioner also preferred Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.38842 of 2019(22) dt.29-01-2026 a Criminal Revision vide Cr. Revision No. 33 of 2018 but the same has also been rejected on 10.01.2019.
sentences._hearing_file: Sanjay Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 29 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel for the opposite party no. 02 submits the petitioner is not paying the maintenance amount which has been fixed by the court below.
sentences._hearing_file: Sanjay Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 29 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: 5. In reply to the aforesaid submission, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the maintenance order was an ex-parte order.
sentences._hearing_file: Sanjay Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 29 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: 6. In the opinion of this Court, for execution of the order granting maintenance/recovery of the maintenance amount, the opposite party no. 02 can take recourse, as per law.
sentences._hearing_file: Sanjay Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 29 January, 2026.json

sentences.text: 7. In view of the aforesaid discussions and in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar reported in (2014) 8 SCC 273 and also in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Gajanan Dattatray Gore Vs. State of Maharashtra and Anr reported in 2025 SCC OnLine SC 1571, this application is allowed.

On 1.8.2017, the informant submitted that she was not properly treated by her in-laws and therefore, the learned SDJM, Gaya cancelled the bail bonds of the petitioner on 24.01.2018, as the same was granted with a condition that the petitioner will keep his wife with full dignity and care.
